critical_code_review_comments: Defensive consistency: get_stock_quote, get_earnings_snapshot, get_health_report, and any other endpoint that returns floats from yfinance should adopt the same NaN/Inf guard pattern (drop NaN rows + per-row try/except). Today only get_stock_history was hardened — the next ex-dividend or split row could surface the same JSON-serialization 500 elsewhere.
Consider centralizing the OHLC-row sanitizer as a small helper (def to_safe_ohlc(row)) so the same logic is reused and unit-testable instead of inlined inside get_stock_history.

The stacked stock card has no top-level data-testid (e.g. stock-card-{TICKER}) — adding one would make full-flow Playwright assertions cleaner; today the test has to rely on stock-details-block-{TICKER}/ai-deep-analysis-{TICKER} as proxies.
App.js still ~1900 lines; the search-then-add-stock orchestration and stacked render loop are good candidates to extract into <StackedStockItem/> as already flagged in iter9.

rca_of_the_issue: ROOT CAUSE: yfinance.history(period='1y') for MSFT included a 2025-05-15 ex-dividend marker row whose Open/High/Low/Close were NaN. FastAPI's default JSONResponse encoder (orjson/json) rejects NaN/Infinity because they are not valid JSON tokens per RFC 8259, raising ValueError 'Out of range float values are not JSON compliant' and surfacing as a 500 from /api/stocks/MSFT/history. App.js fetchStockData uses Promise.all to fan out quote/history/earnings/news/etc., so a single 500 rejected the combined promise and skipped the entire setStackedStocks append — visually the MSFT search-and-click produced nothing. FIX (lines 831-852 of server.py): hist.dropna(subset=['Open','High','Low','Close']) before iterating, plus per-row try/except and safe int(Volume) only when pd.notna(Volume). VERIFIED: 30 backend regression tests + live MSFT frontend flow both green.
